validation.notes: Repaired packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts: migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot() encoded the session-header cwd with cwd.replace(/^[/\\]/, "").replace(/[/:]/, "-"), so Windows drive-letter and UNC cwds kept their backslashes and migrated to bogus directories such as '--C--Users\alice\project--' instead of the canonical '--C--Users-alice-project--' used by getDefaultSessionDirPath() in core/session-manager.ts. The single-line fix adds the backslash to the character class: replace(/[/\\:]/g, "-"), matching the canonical encoder for POSIX, drive-letter and UNC paths (one leading slash/backslash dropped, then every '/', '\' and ':' replaced with '-'). No other production code was touched. .prale-eval/regression.mjs loads the real module through .prale-eval/subject.mjs (loadMigrations with only getAgentDir/stripBom faked, real fs/path) and asserts: POSIX, drive-letter (backslash and forward-slash) and UNC cwds migrate into exactly the canonical sessions/--...-- directory with byte-identical session content and no ':' or '\' in the directory name; malformed/non-session/empty/null headers are ignored and left untouched with no session directory created; a pre-existing destination file is never overwritten and the source is left in place; three consecutive runs are idempotent (no extra directories or duplicated files, bytes preserved). The script exits 0 on the fixed source and fails with AssertionError 'drive-letter session must migrate to sessions/--C--Users-alice-project--/...' when the original encoding fault is reverted (verified by temporarily restoring the faulty line and re-running). Note: repository dependencies are not installed, so `tsc`/`vitest` were unavailable; the regression run above is the focused validation and exercises the real production code, and no dependency install or network access was used.
